submitted.body:
This is the same conjecture as [MathDB 360653](https://mathdb.com/p/360653#s1); it is covered by the same paper, not a separate result.

For every n >= 3 piles and l >= 3 players, the paper constructs a positive initial position where all-GM play makes the first player lose but changing only that player's first move makes that player win. The proof uses the source's monetary payoff and a block invariant giving the exact play lengths. The infinite family is an ordinary proof; the Lean endpoint certifies a finite witness. This same conjecture also appears as MathDB 361128. The two-player theorem is not contradicted.

**Result and scope:** Conjecture 1 fails for every n >= 3 and l >= 3 (ordinary block-invariant proof; Lean certifies (4,4,5)); a computed certificate at (5,5,6) shows no completion of the no-multiple convention rescues it; l = 2 is the GMMV23 theorem

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [GM strategies are not a Nash equilibrium in l-player exact slow NIM(n, n-1) for n, l >= 3: a refutation of Gurvich-Naumova Conjecture 1 (arXiv:2311.03257)](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00055) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00055v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.
